official.deadline_note: No central deadline exists: financing and admission are handled through individually advertised vacancies. NTNU's guidelines for recruitment positions require at least two weeks between announcement and the application deadline. The Faculty of Humanities advertises PhD positions each year with a 1 October deadline (the 2026/27 call closed 1 October 2026); the Faculty of Natural Sciences states there are no fixed application deadlines. Each vacancy carries its own published deadline.
official.application_cycle: Continuous rolling advertisement of individual PhD research fellow positions; at the start of October 2026 NTNU had numerous PhD vacancies open with deadlines from 8 October to 1 December 2026
official.status_note: Available PhD positions are announced at NTNU's web pages and through jobbnorge, and acceptance to a PhD programme is done continuously throughout the academic year and is not restricted to the beginning of term.
official.tuition_coverage_note: NTNU's tuition fee page lists "Doctoral students/PhD students" among the categories exempted from the requirement to pay tuition fees. In addition, PhD candidates in Norway are not considered students and are usually employees of the institution from which they receive their funding.
benefits: Employment as a PhD research fellow (stipendiat) at NTNU, position code 1017, with a gross salary normally NOK 550 800 per annum depending on qualifications and seniority, and a 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund deducted from the salary.

State employee pension rights in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK), which also offers attractive mortgage rates and conditions, and insurance for members of the Norwegian National Insurance Scheme according to Statens personalhåndbok.
Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2) offered by the institution to employees who do not have proficiency in Norwegian, Swedish or Danish at A2 at the time of employment.
Research funds / working capital to implement the project: up to NOK 100 000 at the Faculty of Humanities and research funds up to NOK 150 000 at the PhD programme in Historical and Cultural Studies.
Access to a mentor programme as a new employee at NTNU and to NTNU International Researcher Support (NIRS) for administrative and relocation counselling.

An individual career plan agreed with the employer and followed up in annual employee interviews, access to career guidance throughout the doctoral education, and one hour per week of exercise during working hours.
eligibility: Completed at least five years of higher education that includes a master's degree or other equivalent degree.
A strong academic record and a weighted average for the last two years of the master's degree equivalent to a B or higher in NTNU's grading scale.
A funding plan - financing is an absolute requirement for acceptance to a PhD programme at NTNU.

At least two academic supervisors, with the main supervisor ready when applying, and at least one supervisor (usually the main supervisor) employed at NTNU, which also applies to externally funded candidates.
Education from outside Norway may need NOKUT/HKDIR recognition or a faculty-level assessment; the individual faculty or programme may have set further qualification requirements.

In accordance with the Regulations concerning terms and conditions of employment, former PhD research fellows at NTNU are not eligible for the positions regardless of field of study, and applications from candidates who already have an approved doctorate from other institutions will not be considered.
requirements: Apply for a specifically advertised PhD research fellow vacancy; the application is submitted electronically through the vacancy system (jobbnorge.no), and applications submitted elsewhere will not be considered.
Write the application for admission in cooperation with the main supervisor and submit it to the faculty through the department, using the fixed NTNU application form or the faculty's own form.

A complete application for admission to a doctoral programme must be submitted no later than three months after commencing in the position, and a signed agreement on admission must be available no later than six months after taking up the position.
The project description must be prepared using the faculty's template where one exists (up to 10 pages at the Faculty of Humanities; 5-10 pages at the Faculty of Architecture and Design).
Applicants at the Faculty of Humanities must contact a potential supervisor early and obtain a written confirmation using the faculty's supervisor confirmation template.
A career plan is prepared after appointment, specifying the competence the doctoral research fellow will acquire beyond the doctoral work.
documents: Documentation of former education qualifying you for a PhD: final certificate, diploma and transcript of grades for both the bachelor's and master's degree, officially approved in the country of study, with any diploma supplement and/or NOKUT assessment.
Documentation of the grading scale where it is not clearly shown on the transcript of grades, so that the B-or-higher average can be verified.
An official translation of all academic credentials, produced by a government-authorized translator, public-sector interpreting service or an embassy; translations by the applicant are not accepted.
Documentation of funding for the entire PhD period.

Project description, complete or preliminary (a complete version must be made available within six months of admission if a preliminary one is accepted), accounting for legal or ethical issues and enclosing ethics committee or other approvals where required.

CV, references and testimonials, plus verified documents for applicants educated in countries where verification is required (such as CHESICC for China and HEC for Pakistan) or where paper copies must be sent directly from the institution.
selection_criteria: In the assessment of applicants for doctoral research fellowship positions, emphasis is placed on their qualifications for completing the doctoral education; the assessment is primarily based on documented qualifications, project description, project quality and personal suitability.
An academic assessment is carried out by two internal academic staff with associate professor qualifications.
A recruitment group conducts interviews and reference checks of the most relevant applicants; at least two references must be obtained for each applicant considered for recommendation.
Where there are several qualified applicants, three applicants should usually be recommended and ranked, with reasons given for the ranking.

If any qualified applicant has stated a disability, a gap in their CV or a non-Western immigrant background, at least one applicant from each of these groups must be invited to interview before the recommendation is made.
The appointing authority is the Dean for appointments to recruitment positions, on the recommendation of the Head of Department.
coverage: Gross salary in the position of PhD research fellow, position code 1017, normally NOK 550 800 per annum depending on qualifications and seniority; 2% is deducted as a statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund.

Faculty salary guidelines place all doctoral research fellows at a minimum of NOK 550 800 with 3% salary development per year for up to four years; advertised salary ranges for code 1017 run from NOK 550 800 up to NOK 615 000 depending on competence and experience.
No tuition fee: doctoral students/PhD students are exempted from the requirement to pay tuition fees.
PhD candidates are employees, so living costs are funded through the employment salary under the Norwegian state pay scale rather than through a student stipend.

Project costs - conferences, equipment, books - are covered from research funds/working capital, which vary by faculty and programme (up to NOK 100 000 at the Faculty of Humanities, up to NOK 150 000 in the Historical and Cultural Studies programme).
No separate funding for relocation, flights or accommodation is published; research funds are not intended for the candidate's personal computer.
application_method: Apply to an individually advertised PhD research fellow vacancy on NTNU's vacancy pages or on jobbnorge.no; the application is submitted electronically in that vacancy system.
The application for admission to the PhD programme is written in cooperation with the main supervisor and sent to the faculty through the department.
The process for temporary academic positions is: apply for the position, assessment by a professional committee, interview, approval in advance for admission to a PhD programme, then appointment.
official.application_route: Apply electronically to a specific advertised PhD research fellow vacancy via NTNU's vacancy pages/jobbnorge.no, then secure conditional admission to a doctoral programme with the main supervisor's help.
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality restriction is published for PhD research fellow positions; candidates with external funding or an external workplace must reside at NTNU for at least one year of the doctoral education.
official.international_eligibility: International applicants are eligible; education completed outside Norway must be fully documented and may require HKDIR/NOKUT recognition or a faculty assessment.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The project must fit the discipline of the doctoral programme and the advertising department's research groups; at the Faculty of Humanities the project must be affiliated with one of the Faculty's research groups and the main supervisor must hold a position in one of the departments.
official.research_requirement: A project description is required with the application and is a core part of the assessment; it must account for legal and ethical issues and include any required ethics approvals.
official.duration: Three years of employment as standard; the fixed-term period is three to four years when the position includes career-enhancing work such as teaching
official.description: NTNU's PhD positions are researcher training positions in which the candidate is employed as a doctoral research fellow (stipendiat) in position code 1017 rather than enrolled as a student. Financing is an absolute requirement for admission, and most PhD candidates at NTNU are employed by NTNU or a university college, with individual positions advertised on NTNU's web pages and through jobbnorge.
official.program_type: Doctoral research fellowship (stipendiat) - salaried employment position

not_confirmed: english_requirement - NTNU's central PhD admission pages publish no IELTS/TOEFL or MOI threshold for PhD candidates; the published English test requirements cover international master's programmes and general admission, so no PhD-specific score can be recorded
relocation, flight or installation allowance - no such payment is published for PhD research fellows
an exact application deadline for the current cycle, because each advertised vacancy sets its own deadline and no single central date is published
the exact NOK amount of working capital for most faculties - published figures vary by faculty and programme
verification.notes: Checked NTNU's own PhD admission and financing page, vacancy and benefits pages, faculty salary determination PDFs on i.ntnu.no, current NTNU vacancy advertisements (employer: NTNU) and the recruitment guidelines published on NTNU's knowledge base; the NOK 550 800 figure is stated as the normal gross salary for position code 1017 in current NTNU advertisements and as the minimum starting salary in NTNU faculty salary guidelines.

applicant_utility.summary: Treat every NTNU PhD vacancy as a job advertisement rather than a scholarship: you apply online to one specific position, and the money arrives as a state salary in position code 1017, normally NOK 550 800 gross per year, with no tuition fee and with project money for conferences and equipment that varies a lot between faculties. Because PhD candidates are employees, the salary is taxed and 2% is deducted for the State Pension Fund, so budget a monthly take-home well below a simple 1/12 of the annual figure. The single biggest determinant of success is not your grade point average but whether an NTNU researcher in the relevant group has agreed to supervise your project before you submit - applications that arrive without a willing supervisor rarely survive the first round. Start by identifying the faculty, department and research group your topic belongs to, then email the group before the vacancy appears, since individual advertisements often stay open for only two to four weeks.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Someone with a recent, strong master's degree (a B or better weighted average over the last two years) whose project clearly fits an existing NTNU research group and who is willing to work as an employee rather than a student.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify the faculty, department and research group whose work matches your topic, and contact the group and a potential main supervisor months before the vacancy is published.
Draft the project description in the faculty's own template (Humanities: up to 10 pages; Design: 5-10 pages) and have the supervisor check it before submission.
Obtain the faculty's supervisor confirmation where it is required - the Faculty of Humanities rejects applications without the template-based signed confirmation.

Assemble complete bachelor's and master's transcripts, diplomas, diploma supplements and the grading scale, with translations only from government-authorized translators, interpreting services or embassies.
If you studied in China, Pakistan or one of the countries requiring direct verification, start credential verification (CHESICC/HEC) early because it can take longer than the application window.
Ask HKDIR for a prior recognition statement, or agree with the faculty how your degree will be assessed, if your education system differs markedly from Norway's.
Read the specific advertisement for duty-work percentage, working capital, planned start date and any language documentation it asks for, and confirm you accept a 3-4 year fixed-term contract.
Line up two referees, since at least two references are obtained for anyone recommended for appointment.
common_rejection_risks: No confirmed funding and no main supervisor at the time of application - financing is an absolute requirement and the main supervisor must be in place when you apply.
A project that is not anchored to an advertised department or to one of the faculty's listed research groups, which the committee cannot tie to a supervisor or a research environment.
Being ruled out by the candidate restrictions: former NTNU PhD research fellows are ineligible, and so are candidates who already hold an approved doctorate from any institution.
Recording only a B-minus equivalent average over the final two years of the master's degree, or submitting a record that cannot be converted to NTNU's grading scale.
Missing the short individual deadline - ads commonly run two to six weeks, with no rolling late window.

Submitting the admission paperwork after commencing work: the complete admission application is due within three months and a signed admission agreement within six months, otherwise the basis for the employment lapses.
An incomplete credential file, for example bachelor's documents or the grading scale left out, or a self-made translation.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The position funds living costs through salary and conference travel through working capital, but relocation is on you: flights, shipping, the first month's costs and deposit, insurance before your Norwegian national insurance membership starts, visa and residence-permit handling, and Norwegian tax on the full salary. Semester fees apply only if you take courses beyond the required PhD coursework.
document_audit: Self-translated diplomas or transcripts are not accepted - only government-authorized translators, public-sector interpreting services or embassies.
The whole course of study must be documented from the institution for both the bachelor's and master's level; leaving out bachelor documents is a common gap.
The grading scale must be documented separately if the transcript does not show it, otherwise NTNU cannot verify the B-or-higher average.
Applicants from several listed countries (including China and Pakistan) need credential verification, and some are asked to send paper copies directly from their university - plan for postage time.
At the Faculty of Humanities the supervisor confirmation must use the exact template and be signed and sent as a PDF by the supervisor.
If your master's thesis is not finished you may be assessed with a provisional transcript, but you cannot start without the completed degree.
alerts: Deadlines are per vacancy, not per university: check NTNU's vacancy page and the jobbnorge employer list for NTNU, and expect windows of two to six weeks.
Do not reuse a generic CV - the assessment weights documented qualifications, the project description and personal suitability for completing the doctorate.
Ask in writing which supervisor will be your main supervisor and where they are employed, because at least one supervisor must be employed at NTNU even for externally funded candidates.
Confirm the working capital and duty-work share in the vacancy text, since these differ sharply between faculties and affect both your research budget and your time for the thesis.
Your employment ends if the conditions for the appointment are not met, so enrolment in the doctoral programme after starting the position is a real obligation, not a formality.
Former NTNU PhD fellows and candidates with a completed doctorate are excluded by regulation - check this before investing months in an application.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply electronically to the advertised vacancy on jobbnorge.no (applications elsewhere are not considered); an academic committee of two assessors ranks the applicants, a recruitment group interviews and checks references, and the Dean appoints, after which admission to the doctoral programme is settled with the main supervisor through the department within three to six months of starting.
